sources.note: Nothing on stress or phonology; one paragraph: 'A few words have been secured from the Yokuts. These are indubitably Shoshonean, but not of any known dialect nor wholly of affiliation with any one dialect group... the vanishing trace of a distinctive Shoshonean language and group. The last alternative is by no means precluded; but it may never be proved or disproved.'

sources.citation: Kroeber, A. L. 1907. Shoshonean dialects of California. University of California Publications in American Archaeology and Ethnology 4(3): 65-166. Section 'Giamina', pp. 126-128.
sources.note: Nothing. The entire Giamina record is a 20-word list on p. 128 (tcupu 'house', hewe 'water', pohoim 'road', wadja 'mountain', madjindji 'across', pābahai 'no', xöxinil/xaxinil 'person', muut 'man', wi'ct 'woman', piāt 'deer', ni-ku, bal/bal-aku, bèkt, tabakwan, dab-iku, hahītcu/ahītciwa, em 'much', hüüka 'drink', mik'an 'kill'; numerals 1-6). Page image checked: vowel diacritics only, no accent marks. The words 'accent' and 'stress' do not occur anywhere in the text layer of the whole 1907 monograph; the general phonetic note (pp. 96-100) concerns consonant classes and the ö/ü vowels.
